title: Which Signals of Code Correctness Survive Distribution Shift? Hidden-State and Causal Predictors of Program and Verdict Correctness
abstract: arXiv:2611.07876v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models increasingly judge code, yet without external feedback such judgments are unreliable, and verifying them by executing tests or by extended reasoning is costly. Instead, execution-free correctness predictors use signals from the model's output probabilities, sampled solutions, or hidden states to identify judgments that warrant further verification. However, these predictors may degrade under distribution shifts when generalizing across projects and languages.   We compare six execution-free predictors from four families on Qwen3-Coder-30B and gpt-oss-20b under benchmark shift between LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench and language shift across Python, C++ and Java. We evaluate two targets: whether the model's own verdict on a program can be trusted, and whether the program itself is correct. Besides established approaches, we adapt two novel causal localization methods to code, which have been shown to be more robust

translated_title: 哪些代码正确性信号能在分布偏移下依然有效？程序与判定正确性的隐状态及因果预测器
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于评判代码，但在缺乏外部反馈的情况下，这类判断并不可靠，而通过执行测试或深度推理来验证这些判断的代价高昂。因此，免执行的正确性预测器利用模型输出概率、采样解或隐状态中的信号，来识别哪些判断值得进一步验证。然而，当这些预测器在跨项目、跨语言进行泛化时，可能会在分布偏移下性能退化。我们在 Qwen3-Coder-30B 和 gpt-oss-20b 上，比较了来自四个类别的六种免执行预测器，考察了 LiveCodeBench 与 BigCodeBench 之间的基准偏移，以及 Python、C++ 和 Java 之间的语言偏移。我们评估了两个目标：模型自身对程序的判定是否可信，以及程序本身是否正确。除已有方法外，我们还将两种新颖的因果定位方法适配到代码领域，这些方法已被证明更为稳健。
tldr: 本文系统比较了四类共六种免执行代码正确性预测器在基准与语言分布偏移下的稳健性，并将两种新颖的因果定位方法引入代码领域，同时评估其对程序正确性和模型自身判定可信度的预测能力。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically compares six execution-free correctness predictors from four families—including two novel causal localization methods—under benchmark and language distribution shifts, evaluating their ability to predict both program correctness and the trustworthiness of the model's own verdicts.
